subject: SecOps: hardware validation, upgrade cadence & offline ops next steps
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.m@biotechlabs.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-06T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: SecOps: hardware validation, upgrade cadence & offline ops next steps

Thanks for the time today, Rafael — good discussion. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

Summary of what I captured:
- Deployment mode: Private (air-gapped) appliance hosted in Biotech Labs datacenter; zero outbound egress allowed.
- Workload profile: ~30 concurrent inference sessions, ~120 QPS peak (short-text generation), 8–12k tokens/day aggregate estimate.
- Data residency: on-prem only, retention 90 days for logs, model artifacts managed by client.
- Maintenance windows: ideally Saturday 02:00–06:00 local for firmware/OS patching.

Immediate asks / open items for qualification: 
1) Confirm isolation level (network VLAN vs. physically isolated VLAN + no internet) and whether a locked rack/cabinet is available.
2) Confirm exact power per-rack and PDU redundancy (we need 2x 20A circuits).
3) Provide a point-of-contact for facilities (on-site ops) and the expected lead time for access/escorts.
4) Any corporate policy regarding in-house HSM / KMS for key custody (we support customer HSM, Redwood-managed KMS, or local PKI).

Attachments: redwood-offline-hw-specs.pdf (appliance BOM + sizing), soc2-questions.xlsx (security baseline we discussed).

Proposed next steps:
- Vivek and I will review the facility answers and follow up with a short hardware attestation checklist.
- Schedule a 60-minute engineering workshop (onsite or secure video) to walk through offline upgrade process, acceptance tests, and spare parts SLA. Link to proposed agenda attached.
- If everything aligns, we’ll prepare an SOW draft and a proposed timeline for deployment (4–6 weeks from site approval).

Can you confirm the FACILITIES contact and preferred workshop dates (next week or the week after)?

Thanks,
Laura
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0124

Subject: Re: SecOps: hardware validation, upgrade cadence & offline ops next steps

Thanks, Laura — appreciated. Quick clarifications inline: 

- Isolation: must be fully air-gapped (no outbound egress). We prefer physically isolated VLAN with no bridge to corp internet.
- Power: confirmed 2x 20A per rack is available; UPS on site with N+1 config. I'll send the rack PDU spec later today.
- Facilities POC: Marisa Duarte (marisa.duarte@biotechlabs.com) — she handles escorts and after-hours access.
- HSM/KMS: we plan to use our on-prem HSM for key custody; can you confirm Redwood can integrate with an HSM appliance (PKCS#11)?

Workload notes: Our ML team expects spikes up to 200 QPS for short bursts (10–15 minutes) during batch runs; sustained 120 QPS is accurate. Storage for models + logs ~4TB initially, growth anticipated.

Saturday maintenance window looks good. We can do a workshop next Wednesday 2027-09-15 at 10:00 PT — Rafael + infra lead + Marisa will join.

I’ve attached our internal infra diagram (sent separately to Marisa) and a redacted vendor compliance doc.

-Rafael
Director of MLOps, Biotech Labs
rafael.m@biotechlabs.com
+1 (617) 555-2332

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-09-06T18:10:00-07:00

Adding a few engineering clarifications so the workshop is focused: 

Vivek (Senior Infrastructure) here — a couple items to prep before the workshop: 
- GPU options: we support A6000, H100 and the Ampere 80GB variants. Please indicate preferred GPU family; we’ll size node counts accordingly.
- Upgrade mechanics: for air-gapped sites we offer two methods: (A) signed OS+runtime image on encrypted USB (hand-delivered) or (B) network-isolated PXE from a locked bastion inside the lab. Which is Biotech Labs’ approved method?
- PKI/HSM: Redwood can integrate via PKCS#11; we also support HSM-backed signing for firmware images. Need HSM vendor/model and whether client will allow our signing CA to be present for acceptance tests.
- Spares & RMA: recommend 1 spare GPU and 1 spare NVMe per 4-node cluster on-site for 30-day RTO. Confirm if procurement can stock spares or if Redwood should include pre-staged spares in SOW.

For acceptance tests, we’ll prepare a small offline test harness (CPU/GPU burn, KV cache correctness, artifacts checksum) that can be executed without external network. Sharing a short draft checklist at the workshop.

-Vivek
Director, Infrastructure Engineering
Redwood Inference

To make the session productive, please: 
- Share the exact HSM vendor/model (or confirm "none") before 2027-09-13 so our firmware signing flow can be validated.
- If possible, upload the rack PDU spec and a simple floorplan to the shared folder (I copied Marisa on this thread).
- Confirm whether Biotech Labs will accept signed images delivered on encrypted USB, or if PXE from an internal bastion is required. We’ll prepare both flows but prefer to validate the one you’ll use.

See you in the workshop — Laura
